thread:
sophie: Thinking out loud — we should tie API-key/org rate limits to GPU pool headroom. Static per-key quotas are either overbooking the fleet or leaving GPUs idle. Ideas?

raj: ++ this. dynamic token-bucket seems natural: refill rate scales with headroom. keeps developer quotas but reacts to saturation.

elaine: Proposal sketch: per-org token-bucket (or per-key) for request admission. Refill rate = base_quota * refill_scale where refill_scale is derived from pool headroom and priorities. Use a leaky-bucket at the gateway to smooth bursts.

mike: How do we compute headroom quickly? We need sub-10s signals (available_slots - reserved_pending). Metrics lag is the main risk.

infra-bot: metric snapshot: eu-west-1 pool -> available_gpus=12 queued_jobs=18 active_slots=84

raj: Formula suggestion: refill_scale = clamp(headroom / target_headroom, min_scale, 1.0). Then refill_rate = plan_base_rate * refill_scale. base_rate comes from subscription + SLA. Also weight requests by cost (generate vs embed) so we charge more "tokens" to generation requests.

sophie: Can you show a tiny config example?

raj: Sure — pseudo-yaml:
```
token_bucket:
  scope: org
  base_rate: 10 # req/s default
  burst: 50    # max tokens stored
  weight:
    generation: 1.0
    embedding: 0.2
  dynamic_refill:
    source: pool_headroom_metric
    window_s: 5
    min_scale: 0.1
```

elaine: Gateway behaviour note: differentiate between per-key over-limit (return 429 with X-RateLimit-* headers) and cluster/backpressure (return 503 with Retry-After). If queue is long OR refill_scale < threshold -> prefer 503 to signal operational saturation.

mike: For dedicated/reserved customers: keep a guaranteed bucket (always refill to commit). Add a best-effort spillover bucket for extra capacity. That preserves SLAs.

sophie: Fairness: what stops a single noisy org from starving others?

raj: Weighted fairness + global protection. Track windowed_consumption_pct per-org; if org > 60% of pool for >30s, apply temporary multiplier (0.5) to their refill_scale until they cool down.

elaine: Telemetry: surface refill_scale, tokens_remaining, queue_len, headroom on Console per-pool and per-org. Alert when refill_scale < 0.3 for >1m and queue_len > 50.

mike: Implementation plan: 1) gateway token accounting + dynamic refiller 2) runtime admission -> per-pool queue and early-reject 3) Console metrics & alerts 4) PoC in eu-west for 2 weeks.

sophie: I'll draft a short ADR and spin up a PoC ticket. objections?

raj: :thumbsup:

elaine: +1

mike: 👍
